answer: To stop Sybil attacks, use Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent locks a $5,000 bond in a smart contract. Second, the hardware enclave generates a unique cryptographic identity at the network vertex. Third, the system verifies the hardware signature against a distributed nebula of validator nodes. Finally, any detected fraud triggers immediate slashing. An attacker faces a cost of $50,000 in bonds and 10 days of compute verification per fake node. It is like trying to cross a deep canyon by building a bridge out of expensive, single-use glass bricks that shatter upon misuse.
